why: The statement asks one yes/no question: whether there are infinitely many Mersenne primes. Three events claim to answer it in full (Zaman, Vega's finiteness note, and the Catalan–Mersenne preprint), so their scope is whole. All three are unreviewed, and each shows several F10 signals together: a landmark claim with no uptake for more than two years; later papers (Baker 2026, Wagstaff's 2025 journal paper) that still call the question open; venues that do no review; and internal problems. Vega's abstract calls the question open while claiming to settle it, the same author posted the opposite assumption alongside it, and the note went through patch revisions. The Catalan preprint rests on an unproven generating theorem and shows a lemma and proof that run in opposite directions. So all three are not_credible rather than merely doubtful. The new Mersenne prime and the GIMPS verification milestones are finite instances. The remaining papers are heuristics, statistics, surveys, conditional results, or variants (odd perfect numbers, S-perfect numbers). Baker's ChatGPT acknowledgement covers proofreading only, so its AI role is none.
doubts: The Vega and Catalan full texts were never read; the not_credible calls rest on abstracts, excerpts and context rather than on an identified error. Three ResearchGate infinitude claims were not recorded as events. The Mersenne Star paper has a year-only date of 2025, which still falls after the snapshot.
